outcome: maternal characteristics (BMI, labor duration, blood loss, hospital stay)
cohort: Primigravid Saudi women ≥24 weeks gestation, carrying a singleton pregnancy, aged <35 years, and with no chronic medical problems
finding: The adolescent birth rate was low (20.0 and 16.3 per 1,000 births in 2009 and 2010, respectively), and excluding preterm delivery, adolescent delivery was not associated with a significantly increased medical risk to the mother, fetus, or neonate in this tertiary care setting.
mod_finding: Compared with women aged <16 and ≥16 to 19 years, women aged ≥19 to 35 years had a 42% and 67% increased risk of cesarean section, respectively, and had a 52% increased risk of instrumental delivery.
